types.embedding_query_text: Team: A group of athletes representing a country in international sports competitions Also called NationalTeam, Squad, FootballTeam, SoccerTeam. Examples: Spain's World Cup champions, Argentina, Spain’s women’s side, La Roja.

chosen_type.label: SportsTeam
chosen_type.justification: The definition and examples align with 'SportsTeam' as a group of athletes competing in a sport.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsClub
candidates.comment: A local business or organization dedicated to a specific sport or range of sports, often offering membership and facilities. Also called athletic club, sports association, fitness club. Examples: a local tennis club, a community soccer club, a professional golf club.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and permanent human settlement Also called Metropolis, UrbanArea, Municipality, CapitalCity. Examples: Madrid, Ciudad Rodrigo, Castellana, Cibeles square.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The examples 'Madrid' and 'Ciudad Rodrigo' are cities, matching the schema.org 'City' class.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: ApartmentComplex
candidates.comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being Also called Individual, Athlete, Politician, Celebrity. Examples: King Felipe VI, Pedro Sanchez, Rodri, Lionel Messi.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are individual human names, fitting the schema.org 'Person' class.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific day in the Gregorian calendar Also called Day, CalendarDate, HistoricalDate, EventDate. Examples: 2026-07-20, 2010-07-11, 2023-07-10, 2026-07-19.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are specific calendar dates, aligning with the schema.org 'Date' data type.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

chosen_type.label: AwardTrophy
chosen_type.definition: A physical object awarded to recognize a sporting or competitive achievement
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents a trophy as an award; minting a new type under Product.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.

chosen_type.label: Year
chosen_type.definition: A year in the Gregorian calendar used to denote a temporal period
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are years, and no schema.org class directly represents a year as a temporal unit.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: CourseInstance
candidates.comment: A CourseInstance is a specific offering of an educational course, distinguished by its particular time, location, medium, or target student group. Also called course section, class session, course offering, specific class. Examples: "Fall 2023 Introduction to Python (Online)," "Spring 2024 Art History 101 (Campus A, Section B)," "Summer Intensive Yoga Teacher Training." Distinct from Course, which is the general description of the educational content.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

types.embedding_query_text: Country Examples: Portugal, Morocco, Spain, Moroccan team.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The examples 'Portugal', 'Morocco', and 'Spain' are sovereign states, matching the schema.org 'Country' class.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

chosen_type.label: MediaOutlet
chosen_type.definition: An organization that produces or distributes news or media content.
chosen_type.justification: The example 'Marca' is a media outlet, not covered by existing schema.org candidates; minting under Organization.

candidates.label: MediaReviewItem
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an item or group of items treated as a single unit for evaluation within a MediaReview. Also called reviewed media unit, content item for review, media subject. Examples: a specific viral video, a collection of related images, a particular news clip.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: MediaSubscription
candidates.comment: An intangible service that grants a user access to media content, including audio, video, or books. Also called content subscription, media access plan, digital media membership. Examples: a streaming video subscription, an audiobook service membership, a digital newspaper subscription.

candidates.label: MediaGallery
candidates.comment: A web page that serves as a collection page for various media, such as images, videos, and other multimedia. Also called multimedia gallery, photo and video collection, digital media showcase. Examples: a website's image gallery, a video portfolio page, a mixed-media art exhibition page.

candidates.label: CableOrSatelliteService
candidates.comment: A CableOrSatelliteService is a Service that provides access to media programming, such as TV or radio, delivered via cable or satellite infrastructure. Also called pay TV service, satellite radio provider, broadcast subscription service. Examples: Comcast Xfinity, DirecTV, SiriusXM Satellite Radio.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: OnlineMarketplace
candidates.comment: An OnlineMarketplace, as an OnlineStore, is an e-commerce platform where multiple sellers offer products or services. Also called e-marketplace, digital marketplace, online bazaar. Examples: Amazon, eBay, Etsy. Distinct from OnlineStore, which is a single seller's e-commerce site.
